sections.h2: What should a seller know about Hubbard County?
sections.html:
Hubbard County is in northwestern Minnesota, with Park Rapids as the seat. It was created on February 26, 1883 from part of Cass County and named for Lucius Hubbard, governor from 1882 to 1887. The land is hilly, wooded and dotted with lakes, and parts of Itasca State Park, the Mississippi Headwaters and the Leech Lake Indian Reservation fall inside the county line. The cities are Akeley, Laporte, Nevis and Park Rapids.

The numbers from Census QuickFacts explain why property tax here looks different from the metro:

  • 22,369 residents in the July 2025 estimate, up 4.8% from the 2020 base.
  • 14,900 housing units but only 8,964 households, so a large share of homes are not a full-time residence. The 2020 census counted 39.6% of housing units as vacant.
  • 83.1% owner occupancy, a median home value of $282,600 and a median household income of $71,995.
  • 28.5% of residents are 65 or older.

A cabin or lake home that is used for part of the year is taxed differently from a primary residence, which is why classification is the first thing to check before listing.

sections.h2: Which Hubbard County office handles property tax?
sections.html:
Two departments share the work. The Auditor/Treasurer is responsible for property tax administration, delinquent taxes and the published delinquent tax list, and for forfeitures, repurchases and confessions of judgment. By statute the auditor also sits on the county board of equalization.

The assessor operates inside Property Records at the Government Center, 301 Court Ave., Park Rapids, MN 56470, phone 218-732-3552. Property Records covers valuation and classification, homestead, tax reduction programs and recording of real estate documents, so a single visit can cover a value question and a deed.

sections.h2: When are Hubbard County property taxes due and what are the penalties?
sections.html:
Minnesota Statutes 279.01 sets two halves, payable before May 16 and before October 16 when a parcel's tax is over $100. A parcel at or under $100 is due in full with the first half. A payment mailed and postmarked by the due date is on time, and the treasurer must abate the penalty once if the postmark falls within one business day after.

Late payment penalties under Minnesota Statutes 279.01
StageHomesteadNonhomestead
Day after the due date2%4%
First day of the next monthAnother 2%Another 4%
Each month after, through December1% more1% more
Ceiling8%12%

Agricultural homestead and qualifying farm land can pay the second half through November 15 without penalty. Seasonal residential recreational property that is not used commercially, the statute's class 4c, takes the homestead penalty rates.

sections.h2: How does homestead work for a Hubbard County buyer or seller?
sections.html:
The county has posted a homestead notice for the 2026 assessment. An owner who bought or moved into a home in the past year must apply by December 31, 2026 to have the benefit apply to taxes payable in 2027, and the applicant must have owned and lived in the home by that date. A qualifying relative living there also counts. For residential and agricultural property that list takes in the owner's or spouse's child, grandchild, sibling or parent, plus the owner's uncle, aunt, nephew or niece.

  • Applications can be filed online, in person or by mail, and once granted they are not repeated unless the assessor asks.
  • Every occupant, owner and spouse signs and gives a Social Security number so the state can check that no other Minnesota homestead is claimed.
  • The driver's license must show the home address, since Minnesota requires an address change within 30 days.
  • A relative homestead does not qualify for the property tax refund, and a property that was ever classified seasonal residential recreational under the current owner cannot take a relative homestead.

A seller who moves out or no longer qualifies has to tell the assessor within 30 days. Missing that notice can mean recalculation as nonhomestead and a penalty equal to 100 percent of the homestead benefit.

sections.h2: How do I dispute a Hubbard County valuation?
sections.html:
Talk to the assessor at 218-732-3552 first. Minnesota Statutes 274.01 then gives two stages. The local board of appeal and equalization, which is the town board or city council unless it has handed the job to the county, meets between April 1 and May 31 with at least ten days of published notice. It must finish within 20 days of convening, and its reductions cannot lower the assessor's total by more than one percent.

An owner who skips the local board, after being notified, generally cannot appear before the county board, so missing the spring meeting costs you a step. A late disagreement goes to the county board of equalization, where the auditor serves. Tax Court is the last stop, and a district court petition for a given tax year must be filed by April 30 of that year under Statutes 278.01.

sections.h2: What Hubbard County dates fall in the next few weeks?
sections.html:
• November 15: the last day to pay the second half on qualifying agricultural property without penalty.
  • December: late penalty on unpaid halves keeps growing by 1 percent each month until it reaches the cap for the property type.
  • December 31, 2026: the final day to apply for homestead on a home you owned and lived in during the year.
  • April 30, 2027: the court filing date for a petition about taxes payable in 2027, which follows the March valuation notice.

A seller who closes before December 31 should tell the buyer about the homestead deadline, because the buyer's own application is what carries the benefit into 2027 taxes. The assessor at 218-732-3552 can mail or email the form.

sections.h2: What does a seller need to settle on a Hubbard County sale?
sections.html:
Pay any delinquent tax before recording. Hubbard's recorder asks for this in its recording guidance, and Minnesota Statutes 272.12 stops the auditor from transferring a parcel with delinquent tax on it. Current-year tax is not required at the time of recording unless the parcel is being split, and it is usually collected and paid through the closing settlement. Tax payments are not part of the electronic recording process, so the title company handles the payoff separately.

The recorder accepts abstract and Torrens documents through four trusted submitters: ePN, Indecomm Global Services, Corporation Service Company and Simplifile. State deed tax and mortgage registration tax are collected together with the recording fee. A deed uses an eCRV and, when needed, an electronic well disclosure certificate. For a payoff figure on the current year, ask the Hubbard County Treasurer's Office. Ask the assessor how a lake home is classified, since that decides which penalty rates and homestead rules apply.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Hubbard County property tax?
faqs.a: Payments go to the Auditor/Treasurer at the Government Center in Park Rapids, or through the Pay Your Taxes Online link on the county's I want to Pay page. Mail must be postmarked by the due date.

faqs.q: Does a Hubbard County cabin qualify for homestead?
faqs.a: Only if you own it and live in it as your primary home, or a qualifying relative does. Seasonal residential recreational property is a separate class, and a relative homestead is barred for any property that has been classified that way under the current owner.

faqs.q: When must I apply for Hubbard County homestead?
faqs.a: By December 31, 2026 for the current assessment, which affects taxes payable in 2027. You must own and occupy the property by that date, and applications can be made online, in person or by mail.

faqs.q: Are Hubbard County property taxes paid at closing?
faqs.a: Current-year tax is not required at recording unless the parcel is being split, but it is often settled at closing. Delinquent tax must be paid before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: What is the Hubbard County assessor's phone number?
faqs.a: 218-732-3552, at Property Records, 301 Court Ave., Park Rapids, MN 56470. The office handles valuation, classification, homestead and recording.
